excluded_seen: The first look (look.py, exploratory): the still world and the busy world on side 1,024 from starts 15001 to 15008, read through blocks of 4 to 32. Every bound here was drawn from it, and its rules are the reference rules.

The sizing look (sizing.py, exploratory): the first look's runs again through this study's measures, with the starts learned from and tried on exchanged and halved; and the control world (B2578/S135678) on side 512 from starts 15101 and 15102, read by who leads each block, to see that its leaders stop changing and what the still world's rule makes of it. Its claims were drawn from that.

The search (examples/scale-up-search, exploratory) ran all six rules against their copies on sides 256, 512 and 1,024 from starts 11001, 12001 to 12003 and 13001, and read them by their correlation area and their species' shares: that is how they were chosen. B2/S0 was seen to hold territories from a half-full start only, which is why it starts half full here. Neither the registered test of step 4c nor its sizing ran any of the six.
No run of B24678/S34678, B3568/S124678 or B2/S0 has been read by who leads a block, no coarse rule has been learned from one, and no start from 16001 on has been generated or run.
body.not_tested: On a world's trial starts, at blocks of 16: it keeps growing if its walls at generation 4,096 are at most 0.8 of those at generation 1,024 and at least 5% of its blocks have another leader; it has set if its walls are at least 0.95 of them and at most 2% of its blocks have another leader. A claim about a world that keeps growing is not tested where the world does not; the control's claims are not tested unless the control has set; a claim about a rule run on in a world that keeps growing is not tested through blocks of a size at which more than 0.2 of neighbouring blocks have different leaders at generation 1,024 (territories under five blocks across); and no claim is tested without a number to judge.
body.source: docs/scale-up-plan.md, step 4d and decision D10; the first look in examples/scale-up-closure-territories/look.py
body.statement: Two species with one rule between them, each counting only its own kind, sort into territories that keep growing. Read through blocks by who leads each block: a block changes hands by being surrounded (N); it is the same rule early and late (T); from one block size to the next the rule changes, less on the square clock than on the block clock and less at each rung (R); the first look's rule for a world serves on fresh starts of it (X) and in the other world (B); run on by itself a world's own rule keeps its walls and says where its territories will be (C); the still world's rule serves in three worlds never zoomed out, as it is or at another pace, and runs them on (U); and in a world whose territories set it does not (Z).
body.title: Does a coarse rule stand in for a world of territories, and is it one rule for worlds never zoomed out?
